test.name: Spec 0011 step 7: Keychain dialog after an ad hoc rebuild of stacklyd

expected: After rebuilding stacklyd with ad hoc signing, a user action (secret.reveal from an interactive client) on an item made by the earlier build shows the Keychain dialog, while a background trigger (a start that needs the secret, a client that cannot show a dialog) gets secret.needs_secret or secret.store_access_denied without any dialog, and the observed behavior is noted for each
steps: In a Terminal at the repo root, build both binaries: `cargo build -q -p stacklyd -p stackly-cli`.

Terminal A: start the daemon on the DEFAULT root (no STACKLY_ROOT, so it uses the login Keychain, and it creates ~/Library/Application Support/Stackly if absent): `cargo run -q -p stacklyd`. Leave it running.

Terminal B (a real Terminal, nothing piped, so the client is interactive): `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret set local:user/manual-keychain-check --generate`. Expect exit 0; note whether any Keychain dialog appeared (none is expected for the build that made the item).

Terminal A: press Ctrl-C to stop the daemon. Then `touch apps/daemon/src/main.rs && cargo build -q -p stacklyd` (a new ad hoc build, so a new code identity), and start it again with `cargo run -q -p stacklyd`.

Terminal B: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret reveal local:user/manual-keychain-check`. Note whether the Keychain dialog appears for the item made by the earlier build, and what it says. Click Deny.

Terminal B, a client that cannot show a dialog: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret reveal local:user/manual-keychain-check </dev/null | cat`. Expect no dialog and an immediate failure; note the error code, whether the detail byUser is false, and the exit code.

Terminal B: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret status local:user/manual-keychain-check` and `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret list`. Expect no dialog and the reference listed as present (the probe never reads the value). Note it.
Not covered here: a start that needs the secret (needs instances, feature 10). Write 'not covered' for that part.

Cleanup: `cargo run -q -p stackly-cli -- secret delete local:user/manual-keychain-check`, then `security delete-generic-password -s stackly-secret -a user/manual-keychain-check` (ignore 'could not be found'), then Ctrl-C the daemon in Terminal A.
Write down the macOS version and the exact dialog wording and button labels you saw.
